name: Stinson SM-8A
variants: Related Stinson Junior models (S, R, SR)
summary: Early 1930s four-seat enclosed-cabin high-wing monoplane, one of the first small aircraft with a fully enclosed cabin; the nine-cylinder radial SM-8A is the best-known Junior.

wings: Wing struts also brace the main landing gear legs (outrigger undercarriage)
engines: Nine-cylinder Lycoming R-680 radial, often with exposed cylinders
fuselage: Wide-track outrigger fixed tailwheel gear braced to the wing struts

tellTales: High-wing monoplane with main landing gear braced up to the wing struts
Enclosed cabin behind an exposed nine-cylinder radial
Early 1930s four-seat cabin monoplane with outrigger gear

confusedWith.howToTell: The Reliant is a later, more refined cabin monoplane with a gull wing and a cowled radial; the Junior has a straight wing with outrigger gear braced by the wing struts.
The Robin has two parallel diagonal bracing struts per side and gear mounted to the fuselage; the Junior's landing gear is braced to the wing struts.
The SM-8A is the early radial-powered Junior with outrigger gear; the later R and SR models have a deeper fuselage and a stub wing carrying the struts and gear.
